head: Quick Share app sends files between iPhone, Android and Windows
dek: A new app called Quick Share, not Samsung's or Google's feature of the same name, moves files between Android, iPhone, Windows, Linux and a web browser: free and unlimited on the same Wi-Fi, or as cloud links of up to 1 GB free and 5 GB with Premium at $2.99 a month.
details: On the same Wi-Fi or network, devices find each other and send files directly without a server or an internet connection, to several devices at once, and stopped transfers pick up again. Cloud Transfer makes a link anyone can open, with an optional password; free links show ads, and Premium removes them and keeps links longer. The site says it uses end-to-end encryption and needs no account for local transfers. BetaList names Jump Dong as the maker and featured the app on 21 November.
where: Android (Google Play), iPhone (App Store), Windows (Microsoft Store), Linux (Snap Store) and the web
means: If you often move photos or files between an iPhone and a Windows PC or an Android phone, this is one app for all of them, free when both are on the same Wi-Fi.
todo: Install it on both devices from their app store, or open the web version, and keep both on the same Wi-Fi for free transfers; use a password on cloud links you share.
